title: Detecting a contradiction does not uniquely identify its mechanism
problem: Can a correct additive law on its calibration region conceal an unobserved interaction, and what evidence separates detecting it from explaining it?
failure: All tests below the interaction order agree with the additive baseline. A recovery algorithm assuming a single term can return an inconsistent explanation when two interactions are present; distinct two-term laws can even agree on every discovery input.
correction: Within an exact single-monomial model, all-ones and leave-one-out queries recover the coefficient and interacting subset. Check consistency and choose separating queries for competing models. Classical mixed differences identify pair coefficients on Boolean inputs. Explicitly preserve the hypothesis-class limitation.
transfer: Distinguish anomaly detection, identification within a specified family and invention of a new family. Freeze hypotheses, use unexposed test inputs, and preserve failures. Do not count deterministic synthetic controls as independent cognitive-learning evidence.
limits: Known or calibrated additive baseline, deterministic Boolean oracle, single nonzero hidden term for recovery theorem. 3872 synthetic cases, 35328 anchor checks, 1290584 unused input comparisons, 17118 pair checks. Explicit two-law counterexample. No blinded researcher test, physical causality, novelty or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
